pages.title: CII Business Delegation to Japan
pages.text:
CII Business Delegation to Japan
7-11 September 2026
Register Now
Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) is organizing an exclusive Business Delegation to Japan from 21–25 September 2026, aimed at fostering strategic partnerships and business opportunities between Indian and Japanese enterprises.
The delegation will focus on key areas including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Transformation, Innovation, Smart Infrastructure, IT/ITES, Cybersecurity, Automation, Robotics, Cloud Technologies, and Emerging Technologies. Participants will gain first-hand exposure to Japan's globally renowned innovation ecosystem through interactions with leading government agencies, industry associations, technology companies, startups, innovation hubs, and research institutions.
The programme will include curated B2B and B2G meetings, industry visits, innovation ecosystem engagements, and networking opportunities across Tokyo, Osaka, and Fukuoka. Delegates will have the opportunity to explore technology collaborations, investment opportunities, market expansion prospects, and best practices in digital transformation and innovation.
The mission is designed for industry leaders, entrepreneurs, technology professionals, startups, corporates, investors, and organizations seeking to strengthen their engagement with Japan and explore new avenues for growth and collaboration in one of the world's most advanced technology ecosystems.
Key Focus Areas:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Generative AI
Digital Transformation (DX)
IT/ITES & Cloud Technologies
Cybersecurity & Digital Trust
Automation & Robotics
Innovation & Startup Ecosystems
Smart Infrastructure & Smart Cities
Emerging Technologies & Deep Tech
Dates: 21–25 September 2026
Location: Tokyo, Osaka & Fukuoka, Japan
Join us to explore new business opportunities, build strategic partnerships, and gain insights into Japan's technology-driven future.

CII AI Leadership for CXOs – Scaling AI for Enterprise Value & Transformation 8 September 2026 – 11 September 2026 DoubleTree by Hilton Goa Panaji | Panaji AboutCII AI Leadership for CXOs – Scaling AI for Enterprise Value & Transformation and Industrial VisitsGOA | 8th – 11th September 2026Limited to 30 seats only | Includes accommodation, Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner in DoubleTree by Hilton Goa Panaji* Artificial Intelligence has moved beyond experimentation to become a strategic business imperative. Across industries, organizations are increasingly focusing on scaling AI initiatives that deliver measurable business value, enhance operational efficiency, strengthen decision-making, and create sustainable competitive advantage. As enterprises transition from isolated AI use cases to enterprise-wide transformation, there is an increasing need for senior leadership to understand the strategic, governance, and organizational dimensions of AI adoption.In line with this evolving landscape the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), through CII Digital, remains committed to strengthening industry capabilities through, executive capacity building, industry outreach, policy advocacy and knowledge-sharing initiatives. As part of this commitment, CII Digital is pleased to present “AI Leadership for CXOs – Scaling AI for Enterprise Value & Transformation”, an exclusive executive learning and leadership retreat designed to equip business leaders with the insights and frameworks required to lead AI-driven transformation.The programme will be held in Goa and is designed exclusively for MDs, CEOs, CIOs, CTOs, COOs, Chief Digital Officers, Digital Transformation Leaders, and Business Heads. pages.text:
CII MCED Business delegation to Indonesia Eastern Region 9 September 2026 – 12 September 2026 About

CII Mining and Construction Equipment Division is organising an exclusive Business Delegation to Indonesia from 9 -12 September 2026.

 

Given Indonesia’s strong mineral base, growing infrastructure investment, and rising demand for advanced mining and construction equipment, the Country presents significant potential for business growth and strategic collaboration. Mining sector in Indonesia plays an important role in the global supply chain, particularly in coal and nickel, while ongoing urban development, industrial expansion, and infrastructure projects continue to drive equipment demand. This positions Indonesia as a compelling destination to explore business opportunities, technology partnerships, and collaborations across the mining value chain.

 

Led by Mr Vivek Bhatia , Chairman, CII Mining and Construction Equipment Division, and Managing Director & CEO, TKIL Industries, this delegation aims to promote stronger business ties between India and Indonesia in the mining sector.

 

The objective of the delegation would be:

  • To visit and explore business opportunities at Mining Indonesia 2026, one of Southeast Asia’s leading international mining exhibitions
  • To gain insights into the Indonesian mining, infrastructure, and equipment market and its evolving business landscape
  • To Facilitate direct interactions with leading Indonesian companies and potential business partners
  • Engage with government ministries and relevant authorities to understand policy and investment opportunities
  • Understand global best practices through industry and mine visits

 

The delegation is scheduled to take place from 9 to 12 September 2026. Participants are required to arrive in Jakarta on 8 September 2026. 

 

Key Highlights of the Delegation :

 

  • Visit to Mining Indonesia 2026 – One of the leading international mining exhibitions in Southeast Asia, showcasing the latest technologies, equipment, services, and solutions for the mining industry. The exhibition brings together global manufacturers, suppliers, buyers, policymakers, and industry experts, making it an excellent platform for business networking and market exploration.
  • Exclusive B2B Opportunities – Direct interactions with industry leaders to explore strategic business collaboration opportunities, technology partnerships, and investment avenues.
  • Exclusive B2G Interactions – High-level meetings with State Governments, policymakers and government organizations shaping the mining and resources sector.
  • Sectoral Association Engagements – Dialogues with mine operator associations and industry bodies representing the Mining & Construction Equipment ecosystem.
  • Industry & Site Visits – Visits to leading mining companies in Indonesia to gain insights into global best practices.
Contact UsMMs Disha Chakrabortydisha.chakraborty@cii.in91 33 22307727-28, 22301434Eastern Region Headquarters 6, Netaji Subhas Road Kolkata,West Bengal,India

pages.title: 4th Edition of CII WR Conference on Building Workforce through Upskilling & Reskilling Maharashtra
pages.text:
4th Edition of CII WR Conference on Building Workforce through Upskilling & Reskilling Maharashtra
10 September 2026
Register Now
4th Edition of CII WR Conference on
Building Workforce through Upskilling & Reskilling:
The Human Edge in an AI World
Thursday, 10 September 2026, President - IHCL SeleQtions, Cuffe Parade, Mumbai
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is ushering in a new era of transformation, redefining industries, reimagining business models, and reshaping the future of work. As technologies such as Generative AI, Agentic AI, advanced automation, robotics, and intelligent digital ecosystems mature, organizations are transitioning from traditional operating models to autonomous, data-driven, and hyper-connected enterprises. Across manufacturing, healthcare, financial services, logistics, energy, retail, and professional services, AI is unlocking new opportunities for productivity, innovation, resilience, and sustainable growth.
As businesses accelerate their digital transformation journeys, human capital will remain the cornerstone of long-term competitiveness. While AI can enhance efficiency and augment decision-making, uniquely human capabilities—including critical thinking, creativity, emotional intelligence, adaptability, ethical judgment, collaboration, and leadership—will continue to differentiate successful organizations. The future workforce will require not only digital fluency but also a growth mindset, continuous learning orientation, and the agility to thrive alongside rapidly evolving technologies.
India stands at a pivotal moment in its growth trajectory, with the opportunity to position itself as a global powerhouse for future-ready talent. Realizing this vision will require a collaborative ecosystem that brings together industry, academia, government, and skilling institutions to accelerate workforce transformation. Strengthening industry-academia partnerships, embedding emerging technologies into learning frameworks, advancing lifelong learning, and fostering inclusive talent development will be critical to addressing evolving skill demands and enhancing India's global competitiveness.
In this context, the 4th Edition of the CII Western Region Conference on Building Workforce through Upskilling & Reskilling: The Human Edge in an AI-Powered Future will serve as a strategic platform for thought leadership, collaboration, and action. The conference is scheduled for Thursday, 10 September 2026 in Mumbai and will convene industry leaders, policymakers, academicians, technology pioneers, and HR professionals to explore pathways for building resilient, agile, and inclusive workforces equipped for the AI age.

Regulatory Compliances of
Drug, OTC & Cosmetic Products in Himachal Pradesh
1000 hrs – 1400 hrs, 1 Sep 2026: Hotel Le Mariet, Baddi, Himachal Pradesh
Confederation of Indian Industry is organizing a capacity-building initiative in Himachal Pradesh, aimed at strengthening regulatory understanding, capability building and fostering a greater alignment between industry and regulators.
The initiative is envisaged as an effort to enhance regulatory understanding of drugs, OTC, and cosmetic products, while reinforcing consumer safety and trust. It will serve as a platform for knowledge exchange, focusing on both regulatory expectations and industry best practices.
Key Focus Areas
The programme will cover practical and technical aspects relevant to regulators and enforcement officials, including:
Regulatory compliance requirements under Drugs & Cosmetics Act and Rules including labelling requirements etc.
Formulation science and product safety considerations
Quality control standards and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)
Cosmetic safety frameworks and risk assessment
Responsible industry practices and consumer-centric approaches.
Location: Baddi, Himachal Pradesh
Duration: Half-day event
Participants:
CDSCO officials
Drug Controller
Drug Inspectors
Representatives from the Department of Health

pages.title: 2nd Edition Green Rajasthan Summit 2026
pages.text:
2nd Edition Green Rajasthan Summit 2026
30 September 2026
Register Now
As you may be aware, the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC), a part of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), has been spearheading India's green building movement since 2001. Today, with over 19,830 registered green building projects and a green footprint exceeding 16.05 billion sq. ft., India has emerged as one of the global leaders in sustainable built environment development. This remarkable achievement has been made possible through the continued support and active participation of stakeholders like you.
We are pleased to inform you that CII–IGBC is organising the 2nd Edition Green Rajasthan Summit 2026 on 11 September 2026 in Jaipur under the theme "Climate-Smart Rajasthan: Accelerating Sustainable Growth Through Green Infrastructure". Rajasthan has emerged as a national leader in renewable energy, infrastructure development, tourism, urban growth, and industrial expansion. As the state continues its growth trajectory, there is a growing need to create climate-resilient, resource-efficient, and low-carbon infrastructure that can support long-term economic prosperity while safeguarding natural resources and enhancing quality of life.
Building on the success of its inaugural edition, the 2nd Edition Green Rajasthan Summit 2026 is envisioned as a premier platform bringing together senior leaders from government, urban development authorities, infrastructure agencies, real estate, hospitality, industry, financial institutions, technology providers, and the sustainability ecosystem to deliberate on strategies that can accelerate Rajasthan's transition towards a greener, more competitive, and climate-resilient economy. The Summit will feature leadership discussions, industry perspectives, technology showcases, and strategic dialogues focused on sustainable growth, climate-smart infrastructure, resilient development, and future-ready solutions. The detailed programme outline is enclosed for your kind reference. The programme offers an excellent opportunity to engage with key decision-makers, showcase innovative solutions and best practices, strengthen brand visibility, demonstrate thought leadership, and explore new business opportunities within Rajasthan's rapidly evolving sustainability and green infrastructure landscape.
For More Details, Please contact Mr Nilesh Kumar Rana ( M: 7087190511 | E: Nilesh.rana@cii.in)

pages.title: About us
pages.text:
About us
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) works to create and sustain an environment conducive to the development of India, partnering Industry, Government and civil society through advisory and consultative processes.
CII is a non-government, not-for-profit, industry-led and industry-managed organisation, with over 10,500 members from the private as well as public sectors, including SMEs and MNCs, and an indirect membership of over 365,000 enterprises from 332 national and regional sectoral industry bodies.
For more than 130 years, CII has been engaged in shaping India’s development journey and works proactively on transforming Indian Industry’s engagement in national development. CII charts change by working closely with the Government on policy issues, interfacing with thought leaders, and enhancing efficiency, competitiveness, and business opportunities for industry through a range of specialised services and strategic global linkages. It also provides a platform for consensus-building and networking on key issues.
Through its dedicated Centres of Excellence and Industry competitiveness initiatives, promotion of innovation and technology adoption, and partnerships for sustainability, CII plays a transformative part in shaping the future of the nation. Extending its agenda beyond business, CII assists industry to identify and execute corporate citizenship programmes across diverse domains, including affirmative action, livelihoods, diversity management, skill development, empowerment of women, and sustainable development, to name a few.
For 2026-27, CII has identified “Accelerating Competitiveness: Growth, Resilience, Inclusion, Sustainability, Trust” as its theme, prioritising five key pillars. During the year, CII will align its policy advocacy, institutional initiatives, partnerships, and outreach to support Indian industry in strengthening these five interconnected pillars of competitiveness.
With 70 offices, including 12 Centres of Excellence, in India, and 9 overseas offices in Australia, Egypt, Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, UAE, UK, and USA, as well as institutional partnerships with 255 counterpart organisations in 102 countries, CII serves as a reference point for Indian industry and the international business community.

Economy
Amid a world fraught with persistent geopolitical tensions, rising trade protectionism, and tariff uncertainties, India has navigated global headwinds with remarkable resilience while sustaining an impressive growth trajectory. The IMF’s World Economic Outlook (July 2025) revised India’s GDP growth forecast upward to 6.4 per cent for both 2025 and 2026 by 0.2 and 0.1 percentage points, respectively, reaffirming the country’s position as the world’s fastest-growing major economy. This upgrade underscores India’s capacity to sustain robust momentum despite mounting global challenges.
As per MoSPI’s estimates, the Indian economy grew by 6.5 per cent in FY25. While this marks a moderation from 8.8 per cent average growth achieved over the past three years, the performance remains impressive against a turbulent global backdrop. India’s growth in FY25 has been underpinned by strong domestic consumption, which accelerated to 7.2 per cent from 5.6 per cent in the previous year. A key driver of this surge has been robust rural demand, supported by a buoyant agricultural sector. Favourable monsoon boosted agricultural output and bolstered rural incomes, lifting consumption while keeping the inflation benign. Thus, the combination of strong consumption and robust agricultural performance has emerged as a critical pillar of India’s growth momentum, despite moderation witnessed in manufacturing growth. The services sector has also provided impetus to the economic growth, with exports remaining robust even as merchandise exports softened due to weak global demand.
Looking ahead, the outlook for the Indian economy in FY26 remains strong. A good monsoon and healthy kharif sowing are expected to keep inflation anchored and consumption buoyant. India also maintains critical buffers in the form of robust services exports and healthy foreign exchange reserves, which provide insulation against global volatility. On the policy front, proactive government measures, including recent announcements of GST 2.0 reforms and formation of a task force for carrying out next-generation reforms, are set to enhance ease of doing business, simplify compliance, and stimulate private consumption and investment. These strengths will continue to reinforce India’s growth trajectory even in the face of global uncertainties. This will lend strength to India’s growth trajectory over the medium-term as well.

Consulting / Advisory Services
Feasibility Analysis and Reporting Services for MSMEs
CII offers Feasibility Analysis and Reporting Services for MSMEs to enable MSMEs to prepare proposals for funding or Joint Ventures. This service is being provided using a Computer model for Feasibility Analysis and Reporting (COMFAR) software developed by UNDO. This software permits the user to simulate the short- and long-term financial and economic situation of investment projects. The software facilitates the analysis of industrial as well as non-industrial projects, whether new investments, rehabilitations, expansions, joint venture or privatization projects.
Lean Six Sigma
Over several decades, quality philosophy has evolved from “Inspecting the Quality into the Product” to “Right the first time” and building “Robust Products and Processes” which finally lead to a “Zero Defect” output. While various quality gurus propagated different approached, the key objectives of the programs remained quite similar. Lean Six Sigma is one of the philosophy which addresses some of the key requirements in today’s environment • Business Results and Breakthrough Improvements • Data Driven with Application of Right Tools • People Involvement and Capability Building • Structured Execution and Review Mechanism CII Institute of Quality focuses on customising the approach to the specific industry requirement and builds capability to ensure sustained results. The CII Institute of Quality initiated support to industry on the subject almost a decade back and since then serviced 200 organisations and certified 220 Black Belts.
Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) & Lean Management
Total Productive Maintenance, shortly termed as TPM, is the concept originated and developed by Japan Institute of plant Maintenance (JIPM) Tokyo, since late sixties. JIPM-TPM is the key for the operational excellence for many Japanese companies. TPM strives to achieve high level of productivity, through total participation of all people inside the organisation and then developing self-managing abilities in people and practices. Productivity, in JIPM-TPM means increasing production and reducing cost simultaneously.
Quality Management & Laboratory Services

CII-EXIM Bank Award for Business Excellence
The Award for Excellence was established jointly by CII and Export-Import (EXIM) Bank of India in 1994 and is based on the EFQM Model for Excellence. Its main aim is to enhance the ‘Competitiveness of India Inc.’, and recognises organisations who have achieved excellence. A large number of organisations have used this model to: • Define excellence across the organisation • Develop an integrated approach for achieving substantial competitiveness • Review and improve strategy, process and performance • Identity and share first-class practices • Provide opportunities to develop business leaders.

International
CII International serves as the global engagement arm of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), dedicated to strengthening India's economic partnerships with the world. It acts as a vital bridge between Indian industry and the international business community by fostering strategic dialogue, facilitating trade and investment, and promoting long-term economic cooperation.
Working closely with governments, industry associations, multilateral institutions, think tanks, academia and global businesses, CII International creates platforms for meaningful interactions through high-level business forums, CEO roundtables, trade and investment missions, conferences, seminars, exhibitions and sector-specific dialogues. It also facilitates interactions between Indian industry and visiting Heads of State and Government, Ministers, policymakers and senior business leaders, helping forge and further strengthen international economic partnerships.
With a strong domestic presence through 70 offices across India, including 13th Centres of
Excellence, and an expanding international footprint through 9 overseas offices in Australia,
Egypt, Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, the UAE, the United Kingdom and the United States, CII provides Indian enterprises with unparalleled global outreach. Complementing this network are institutional partnerships with over 255 counterpart organisations across more than 100 countries, making CII a trusted partner for businesses seeking to explore international markets, forge strategic alliances and access global opportunities.
CII International remains committed to advancing the priorities of Indian industry by promoting international trade, facilitating investments, supporting global value chain integration, encouraging technology and innovation partnerships, and contributing to policy dialogue on emerging global economic issues. Through its extensive network and sustained engagement, CII International continues to strengthen India's position as a trusted global economic partner while enabling Indian businesses to compete, collaborate and grow on the world stage.

Development Initiatives
A key concern for policy makers and industry is to include Indians from all strata of society in the country’s impressive growth story. At the present, the majority of the population remains at the periphery of development. India’s growth story has captured the world’s attention and admiration. However, we cannot in all conscience begin to celebrate the Indian success story while a majority of our 1.1 billion people still live in poverty. There are disparities amongst regions, states, sectors, and communities. Amongst the States, the North-Eastern and the central regions, which have large tribal populations, are lagging behind. Amongst sectors, agriculture has fallen behind industry and the service sector. Religious minorities, large sections of Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribal (ST) groups, and women still do not have access to many job opportunities and human development. While the top end of the economy is experiencing phenomenal wage growth, the informal sector, which is the largest job creator for the country continue to be characterized by low wages and income insecurity. Public health indices for India continue to stagnate at very low levels with large- scale incidence of malnutrition. There is need to address these issues with urgency. We are way behind if we assess ourselves against the Millennium Development Goals set up by the United Nations. India can move up on these parameters only if every segment of civil society comes forward to forge “public-private-people partnerships”. Each segment of society has competencies that the other needs, to achieve its goals. Pooling resources such as knowledge, finances, infrastructure, technologies etc. can hasten the process of reaching out to those that are at the bottom of the pyramid.
CII has been in the forefront of bringing in economic change and has been playing a significant role in the formation of a new and competitive India. It was almost 15 years ago that CII realized that all round evelopment was essential for sustaining the growth process and role that Corporates can play a major catalytic role in bringing this about, expanding the coverage of creation of wealth and catalyzing social change. Over the years, CII’s agenda has, therefore, expanded to include “inclusiveness” and “sustainability” over and above its running theme of “competitiveness”. The imperative for inclusive growth needs no repetition in the context of India's long-term growth prospects. Interestingly, a noticeable shift in policy is being materialized in policy making from subsidy-based programmes to those enabling more income generation. In a parallel process, voices in this debate for marrying market elements with social objectives are gaining strength. Encouragingly, there is a growing consciousness and conviction amongst companies that businesses have dual roles - to create shareholder value and as well play a proactive role in the community in the environment in which they operate. This is where we see a CII role in creating new partnerships for development, especially between wealth creators and the NGO community and Self Help Groups in catalyzing win-win growth stories. To achieve equitable, inclusive growth, the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), seeks to bring in social transformation through a complete programme of policy advocacy, knowledge creation, knowledge dissemination and “on-ground” model projects. Through a series of focused interventions, CII hopes to mainstream economically and socially challenged groups and draw them into a cycle of growth, development and empowerment. All these interventions are undertaken under CII’s broad canvas of “Development Initiatives”.

How India Inc. can help unmask our cities, make the air cleaner

Ayushman Bharat is a Fertile Ground for Inter-Sectoral Collaboration

pages.title: CII Centres of Excellence
pages.text:
Centres of Excellence
Since 1995, CIIs centenary year, CII has been creating Centres of Excellence with the objective to:meet a huge unmet need of industry and the society at large that can be met through capacity and capability development nurture experts who are skilled and trained on state of art technologies have a long term focus in building competitiveness in the centre and in their stakeholders. The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Centres of Excellence, catalyse and facilitate to create and sustain capabilities and competitiveness of organizations with a view to impact the Indian society through training, consulting, advise and research to the industry, government  in India and Overseas.CII Centres of excellence provide special advisory services that can benefit an organization in public or private sector(Large, medium, small and Start-ups, government departments, Financial & Educational Institutions and NGOs).  These centres of excellence enjoy the trust of their 2000 + customers in India and more than 100 International clients.With 62 offices, including 10 Centres of Excellence, in India, and 8 overseas offices in Australia, Egypt, Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, UAE, UK, and USA, as well as institutional partnerships with 350 counterpart organizations in 133 countries, CII serves as a reference point for Indian industry and the international business community.These centre of excellence provide Specialised Services to build Leadership, Strategy for Sustainability, Identify and Adapt Clean Technologies and Management, Enhance Energy efficiency and become Environment friendly, adopt world class practices in Logistics and Manufacturing Management through the Japanese approach: TQM, TPM, TOC, Lean, Six Sigma, VLFM) and Western approach (M.Sc in Engineering Management with WMG, UK) and help to benchmark for Business Excellence. One of the Centres is dedicated to competence building for SMEs through the cluster approach, and this centre is a one stop shop for this priority sector. These Centres of Excellence are located as follows:CII Institute of Logistics, ChennaiCII Institute of Quality, Bangalore CII - ITC Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Development, DelhiCII-Centre of Excellence for Competitiveness for SMEs CII - Naoroji Godrej Centre of Manufacturing Excellence, MumbaiCII - Sohrabji Godrej Centre of Excellence, HyderabadCII - Suresh Neotia Centre of Excellence, KolkataCII - Triveni Water Institute, GurugramCII - FACE, New DelhiCII Centre of Excellence for Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Start-upsCII Centre for Women LeadershipCII Centre of Excellence on Employment & LivelihoodCII – Rahul Bajaj Centre of Excellence on SkillsThe services range from providing networking opportunities with other business organizations, institutions, governments, political and business leaders; participation in industrial and business missions; seminars, training programmes, conferences; opportunities to involve in social sector activities.

pages.title: CII FOUNDATION
pages.text:
CII FOUNDATION
The CII Foundation was set up by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in 2011 and works across India through a collaborative approach, partnering with Government, corporates, civil society and NGOs, academic institutions, and other key stakeholders to drive social change.
The Foundation undertakes projects in diverse areas, often on a pilot basis initially, and presents a successful model of engagement that is replicable and scalable to amplify impact. Each initiative is led by a committed team of dedicated stakeholders who bring different expertise to the initiative for maximum impact.
As a Foundation, the CII Foundation is uniquely placed to leverage the vast network of CII’s Membership to transform lives.
Vision
Enable Industry for Infusing Inclusive Development
Mission
The CII Foundation works towards inclusive development by designing and implementing high-impact projects to cover some of the most marginalised communities, working closely with marginalised communities and donors, especially the Corporate Sector.

Key Initiatives
Climate Change - Crop Residue Management
The initiative is a community-driven field intervention to mitigate stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana, which is a leading cause of air pollution and soil degradation.
Designed in a participatory approach, this multistakeholder project is being rolled out with the support of government, agricultural universities and major corporate supporters such as Apraava Energy, Goodyear, Fidelity International, PTC India Financial Services, HDFC Bank, JSW Foundation, Cadence Design Systems and SBI Card.
Under this initiative, farmers are supported through in-situ and ex-situ methods to adopt environment friendly alternatives to stubble burning through a gamut of interventions.
Early Childhood Education
The CII Foundation focuses on improving the quality of early childhood education (ECE) for children aged up to 6 years, delivered through the Anganwadi Centres (AWCs). Several Centres have infrastructural issues and are poorly equipped to impart quality education to this age group. Adopting a multi-stakeholder approach focused on improving childcare and developmentally appropriate environment for children, the CII Foundation works with corporates such as BlueStar Limited, Volvo Group Trust and local NGOs to identify and work with AWCs across India, leading to a positive impact on the quality of learning and increased attainment of learning outcomes for children.
Healthcare
Raising health awareness, improving healthcare infrastructure, and building capacity of healthcare professionals are crucial steps towards creating healthy and resilient communities.
The CII Foundation is committed to strengthening healthcare systems across the country. We have launched several initiatives in collaboration with various key stakeholders to improve healthcare infrastructure and delivery. We adopt a community-centred strategy to improve overall health and nutrition outcomes with a focus on women and child health.
Livelihood and Skilling
To drive holistic rural development, a comprehensive scoping exercise was undertaken to design and pilot integrated village development initiatives focusing on skilling and livelihoods. The study was conducted across Barabanki and Chandauli (Uttar Pradesh), Gumla (Jharkhand), the Sundarbans (West Bengal), and Gummidipoondi (Tamil Nadu) to identify key areas of intervention and tailor impactful programs for these communities. Pilot interventions include rural women livelihood initiatives and soft skills training for youth in the identified villages.
Women Empowerment
The CII Foundation Woman Exemplar Program recognizes exemplary women working at the grassroots. The program, since its inception in 2005, promotes women’s empowerment at the community level by discovering, recognizing and supporting those who have, against all odds, excelled and contributed significantly to the development process in India.
The women are recognized through the Woman Exemplar Award in four categories – Education, health, Micro-enterprise and Community Strengthening. Intensive capacity building is undertaken for the Exemplars through training and workshops to help them accelerate and amplify their social impact.
Waste Management
To address the challenges posed by inefficient waste management which aggravates pollution and results in poor health of the people, the CII Foundation leads transformative waste management projects across diverse landscapes such as Delhi, Kerala, Haryana, and Leh working in partnership with government, corporates such as HDFC Bank and General Insurance Corporation of India and local communities. The multi-stakeholder projects are community led and complement the government initiatives to promote efficient waste collection, processing, recycling and disposal to create zero-waste neighbourhoods.
For more details, visit www.ciifoundation.in

pages.title: CII Eastern Region
pages.text:
CII Eastern Region
The Confederation of Indian Industry Eastern Region (CII ER) comprises of the states of Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Orissa and West Bengal. The Eastern Region witnessed substantial economic growth in recent times and is now booming with confidence. The eastern region of India is a land of huge potential and is endowed with plenty of rich minerals, forests, productive and fertile soil and rich cultural heritage. Given the available natural resources and quality manpower, the key growth engines in this part of the world are Iron & Steel, Power, Mines & Minerals, Tourism, Agro & food processing, Infrastructure, IT & ITES, Petrochemicals, Leather, Real Estate, Retail and Cement. The Eastern states have potential for large-scale production and export of spices, jute, and other agro products. A spurt in investments coming to these states is an indication of a bright future for trade and industry in the region. There has been a continuous improvement in the hard and soft infrastructure. The growth of IT & ITES, Healthcare and Tourism in the eastern states coupled with rapidly developing educational sector unfolds unique advantage adding to the rich intellectual base of the region. The CII National Theme for 2023-24 was decided as Towards a Competitive and Sustainable India@100: Growth, Inclusiveness, Globalisation, Building Trust. Dovetailing with the national theme, the states and the region have decided to work on the theme of EAST - Economic Action for a Sustainable Tomorrow. The states have taken up three priority areas for the year focusing on Competitiveness, Sustainability, Growth, Livelihood and Inclusion, Globalisation and Building Trust and have committed to work in these spaces. They are working extensively with the CII Centres of Excellences and would make strong cases of advocacy to their governments in various verticals apart from the various initiatives they would undertake in the year.

In addition to the above, the Council has been regularly organizing programs covering different issues & subjects for the benefit of our members. pages.title: CII Membership
pages.text:
Membership
About Membership
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) works to create and sustain an environment conducive to the development of India, partnering Industry, Government and civil society, through advisory and consultative processes.
CII is a non-government, not-for-profit, industry-led and industry-managed organization, with around 9,000 members from the private as well as public sectors, including SMEs and MNCs, and an indirect membership of over 300,000 enterprises from 286 national and regional sectoral industry bodies.
For more than 125 years, CII has been engaged in shaping India's development journey and works proactively on transforming Indian Industry's engagement in national development. CII charts change by working closely with Government on policy issues, interfacing with thought leaders, and enhancing efficiency, competitiveness and business opportunities for industry through a range of specialized services and strategic global linkages. It also provides a platform for consensus-building and networking on key issues.
Extending its agenda beyond business, CII assists industry to identify and execute corporate citizenship programmes. Partnerships with civil society organizations carry forward corporate initiatives for integrated and inclusive development across diverse domains including affirmative action, livelihoods, diversity management, skill development, empowerment of women, and sustainable development, to name a few.
As India strategizes for the next 25 years to India@100, Indian industry must scale the competitiveness ladder to drive growth. It must also internalize the tenets of sustainability and climate action and accelerate its globalisation journey for leadership in a changing world. The role played by Indian industry will be central to the country's progress and success as a nation. CII, with the Theme for 2023-24 as 'Towards a Competitive and Sustainable India@100: Growth, Inclusiveness, Globalisation, Building Trust' has prioritized 6 action themes that will catalyze the journey of the country towards the vision of India@100.
With 65 offices, including 10 Centres of Excellence, in India, and 8 overseas offices in Australia, Egypt, Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, UAE, UK, and USA, as well as institutional partnerships with 350 counterpart organizations in 133 countries, CII serves as a reference point for Indian industry and the international business community.

pages.title: CII Awards & Recognition
pages.text:
CII Awards and Recognitions
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), through its Competitiveness Development Services, recognizes and celebrates organizations that demonstrate exceptional performance, innovation, and leadership across diverse sectors. The CII Awards provide a prestigious platform to honour Indian industry that have consistently set benchmarks in operational excellence, business performance, sustainability, and organizational transformation.
Spanning a wide spectrum of industries and functional domains, the CII Awards portfolio encompasses categories that recognize excellence in Business Excellence, Quality Management, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), Low Cost Automation, Manufacturing Practices, Energy Management, Environment, Health & Safety (EHS), Logistics & Supply Chain, Food Processing, Water Management, Digital Transformation, Design, Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), Innovation & Entrepreneurship, Leadership, Sustainability, Green Business, Skill Development, Industry 4.0, Robotics & Automation, Diversity & Inclusion, Disability Inclusion, Gender Parity, Affirmative Action, Circular Economy, Green Buildings, and several sector-specific and regional excellence awards. In addition, CII organizes specialized competitions and recognition programmes focusing on Kaizen, 5S, Quality Circles, Safety Practices, Digitalisation, Lean Manufacturing, and other continuous improvement initiatives.
These awards are designed to recognize organizations of all sizes—from MSMEs and startups to large enterprises—for adopting global best practices, driving innovation, improving competitiveness, and creating sustainable value for stakeholders. By showcasing exemplary achievements across diverse categories, the CII Awards inspire organizations to pursue continuous improvement, accelerate transformation, and contribute to the growth of a globally competitive and future-ready Indian industry. Explore the various award categories below to learn more about their objectives, eligibility criteria, and application process.

CII Roles
Roles
Our primary goal is to develop Indian industry and to ensure that government and society as a whole, understand both the needs of industry and its contribution to the nation's well being. For this, we work
To identify and strengthen industry's role in the economic development of the country
To act as a catalyst in bringing about the growth and development of Indian Industry
To reinforce industry's commitment to society
To provide up-to-date information and data to industry and government
To create awareness and support industry's efforts on quality, environment, energy management, and consumer protection
To identify and address the special needs of the small sector to make it more competitive
To promote cooperation with counterpart organisations
To work towards the globalisation of Indian industry and integration into the world economy
This is done by adopting a proactive and partnership approach with the government on various national and international issues concerning the Indian economy. It closely interacts on policy issues at both the central and state levels. Extensive dialogue and interaction with members and all sections of the community to build consensus are held.

pages.title: CII History
pages.text:
CII History
History
The history of CII is the story of the
transformation of a miniscule association, representing a small segment
of industry, to the premier business association of modern India.
The journey began in 1895 when 5
engineering firms, all members of the Bengal Chamber of Commerce and
Industry, joined hands to form the Engineering and Iron Trades
Association (EITA).
Engineering and Iron Trades Association (EITA) - 1895
EITA was set up at the end of 1895 with the
aim of pressurising the colonial government to place government orders
for iron and steel and engineering goods with companies based in India.
At that time the practice was to place all government orders with firms
based in UK.
Indian Engineering Association (IEA) - 1912
The change
in name from
EITA to IEA in 1912 reflected the association's decision to exclude
traders from the membership and concentrate fully on promoting the cause
of manufacturers. By this time, many more manufacturers had come into
being and there was a conflict of interest between traders, who
preferred government orders to be placed with companies in the UK, and
manufacturers of engineering goods, who sought industry promotion
through public orders.
Engineering Association of India (EAI) - 1942
Till 1942 IEA
was the only all-India association of engineering industry and
represented mainly big engineering companies, particularly the British
firms. This led to a situation where the interests of the Indian firms
(mainly medium and small scale) were not sufficiently represented. Thus
the Engineering Association of India (EAI) was established in 1942 as an
affiliate of the Indian Chamber of Commerce. EAI represented small and
medium engineering firms mostly owned and promoted by Indians, and had
different origins and management styles from the IEA.
Association of Indian Engineering Industry (AIEI) - 1974
After Independence of
India in 1947, the
public sector assumed the lead role in industrial development. By 1970s,
a new base of heavy industries had been built, but private companies
faced restrictions through licensing requirements for new units and /or
expansion. Keeping in view the greater interests of the Engineering
industry in the country, in April 1974, the two associations - IEA and
EAI - merged to form the Association of Indian Engineering Industry
(AIEI). For the engineering industry the merger meant a stronger
association capable of harnessing larger resources and providing a wider
range of services.
Confederation of Engineering Industry (CEI) - 1986
Foreseeing the upcoming
challenges in
the future, the leadership at AIEI felt the need for greater
consolidation and solidarity that would put the industry on a stronger
footing and would help it meet the challenges of competition and
globalisation. Thus in 1986 there was a change in name from AIEI to the
Confederation of Engineering Industry (CEI), reflecting the growth and
expansion of the organisation since 1974. CEI now became an apex body
for manufacturing industries at the national level.
Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) since - 1992
In 1991, industrial
licensing was abolished
and economic reforms on a wide scale started taking shape. With effect
from 1st January 1992, in keeping with the government's decision to opt
for the liberalisation of the Indian economy, the name of CEI was
changed to Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). In a new policy
environment, it was natural that there would be inter-sectoral
integration through a process of diversification and expansion, where
the engineering units would diversify into non-engineering units and
vice-versa.
Since 1992, through rapid expansion and consolidation, CII has grown to
be the most visible business association in India.

CII Leadership
Mr R Mukundan
President, CII (2026-27)and Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Limited
Dr (Mrs) Suchitra K Ella
President Designate,CII (2026-27) and Co-Founder & Managing Director, Bharat Biotech International Limited
Mr Shashwat Goenka
Vice President,CII (2026-27) and Vice-Chairman, RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group
Mr Chandrajit Banerjee
Director General, CII
Over the years, leaders at the helm of CII have proved themselves to be visionary industrialists. They have been able to anticipate changes in the economic environment, identify emerging challenges and evolve action-solutions for development. A unique feature of CII has been a constant reinvention of itself into an institution that today is not only leading industry, but working for the progress of the nation as a whole.
At critical turning points in the country's economic history, CII's leaders have demonstrated the courage to lead Indian industry into uncharted territories and engineer change. CII leaders have consistently promoted a policy of partnership and cooperation with all stakeholders, and particularly with the Government. This intrinsic partnership approach has played a major role in the evolution of Indian industry over the years, as it transformed from a frail entity insulated from the global economy into a strong and vibrant sector that is driving India's economic growth today.
The key positions of leadership in CII are President, President Designate, Vice President. For 2026-27, Mr R Mukundan, Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Limited, is the President of CII; Dr (Mrs) Suchitra K Ella, Co-Founder & Managing Director, Bharat Biotech International Limited, is the President Designate of CII; while Mr Shashwat Goenka, Vice-Chairman, RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, is the Vice President of CII.
The CII Secretariat is headed by the Director General who oversees the implementation of action agendas and leads the day-to-day management and operation of this vast organisation. Mr Chandrajit Banerjee is the Director General of CII since 2008 with an experience of over 35 years in CII.

pages.text:
Chandrajit Banerjee
Director General, CII
Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)
23, Institutional Area
Lodi Road
New Delhi-110 003
Tel: +91-11-2462 1874
Fax: +91-11-2463 3168
Email: info@cii.in
Website: www.cii.in
Chandrajit Banerjee (CB) is the Director General (DG) of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). CII is India’s apex industry organisation, proactively enhancing the competitiveness of Indian Industry.
CB has been with CII for almost 40 years and has been serving as its Director General since 2008. In this post, he is responsible for the overall operations of CII.
CB is a Member of a number of important Government advisory bodies at the national and state levels. As DG of CII, he leads and contributes to many policy level dialogues / discussions to enhance the competitiveness of Indian industry and towards the economic development of India.
He holds / has held Trusteeship and Board Member posts in many institutions including Institute of Economic Growth (IEG); Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), Bharatiya Yuva Shakti Trust (BYST); Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM); World Economic Forum (WEF) Global Agenda Council of India; Commonwealth Enterprise and Investment Council (CWEIC) etc. He is also a Member of the Managing Committee of SPORTSCOM and Governing Council Member of Sector Skill Councils. CII Foundation and India@100 Foundation, which are promoted and supported by CII, are also institutions where CB is a Board member. CB is also a Director of Singapore India Partnership Foundation (SIPF). He is a Director on the Board of “Invest India” which is set up by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.
He is also Secretariat for many bilateral CEOs Forums constituted by the Government of India such as Australia, France, Malaysia, Indonesia, Japan, Sweden, South Africa and many more.
Prior to his appointment as Director General, CB held several leadership positions in key areas including sectoral verticals of manufacturing, services, agriculture and life sciences as well as the small and medium enterprise (SME) sector. He has also led CII’s policy work relating to macroeconomic policy, financial services and corporate governance.
He was the first Executive Director of the National Foundation of Corporate Governance (NFCG), an organisation set up by the Government of India.
CB has been honoured with the Special National Level Awards “Knight” order and other Highest level civilian awards by a few important and significant countries. These have been bestowed on him for his International relations and connects to promote economic collaboration.
He has been honoured with Honorary Doctorate (D. Phil Honoris Causa) and Honorary Doctorate in Business Management from some leading National level Universities / Institutions.
Chandrajit Banerjee is a Post-Graduate (MS) in Economics with specialisation in Economics of Planning and Econometrics from the University of Calcutta. Earlier, he did his graduation from St. Xavier's College (Calcutta) in Economics (Hons).
As an apex industry body, CII works closely with the Government of India and industry to create and sustain an environment conducive to the development of India. CII is a non-government, not-for-profit industry-led and industry-managed organisation serving directly and indirectly 365,000 enterprises, both private and public sectors, including SMEs and MNCs. More than 332 national and regional sectoral and industry bodies are members of CII. CII has over 600 sectoral and subject-based committees and other groups to advance policy issues for the country and focus on competitiveness of Indian industry.
With around 70 offices, including 12 Centres of Excellence, in India, and 9 overseas offices in Australia, Egypt, Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, UAE, UK, and USA, as well as institutional partnerships with around 255 counterpart organisations in 102 countries, CII serves as a reference point for Indian industry and the international business community. The CII Centres of Excellence offer a range of services for Indian industry in the areas of quality, manufacturing excellence, green building and energy conservation, water, logistics, leadership management, competitiveness, sustainable development, food & agriculture, and innovation, entrepreneurship & start-ups.

pages.title: CII Strategies
pages.text:
About us
Strategies
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) serves as a catalyst for India's
economic transformation by partnering with industry, government and society to build
a globally competitive, sustainable and inclusive economy. Guided by the vision of
Viksit Bharat, CII's strategy is anchored in five core functions—
Policy Reforms, Competitiveness, International Engagement, Business Development
and Community Development—that collectively strengthen the business ecosystem
and enable industry to contribute meaningfully to national development.
At the heart of CII's strategy is a collaborative approach that brings together
governments, businesses, academia, civil society, multilateral institutions and global
partners to address emerging opportunities and challenges. By fostering policy dialogue,
promoting innovation and competitiveness, facilitating international partnerships,
enabling business growth and advancing inclusive development, CII creates platforms
that generate shared value for industry, society and the nation.
Policy Reforms
Policy advocacy is at the core of CII's mission to create an enabling business
environment that supports India's economic growth and global competitiveness. Working
in close partnership with the Central and State Governments, CII facilitates continuous
government-industry dialogue to ensure that policy formulation is informed by industry
insights, evidence-based research and global best practices. Through constructive
engagement with policymakers, business leaders, academia and thought leaders, CII
contributes to the development of policies that promote investment, innovation, ease
of doing business, sustainable development and inclusive growth.
This engagement is anchored in CII's robust institutional framework, led by the
National Council—the organisation's highest governing body—along with its
National Committees, Sector Councils, Regional and State Councils, and Centres of
Excellence. These strategic platforms foster dialogue, build consensus across
industries and regions, and enable the formulation of balanced policy recommendations
that reflect the collective voice of Indian industry.
Competitiveness
Enhancing the competitiveness of Indian industry is central to CII's mission of
building globally competitive, future-ready enterprises. Through its Centres of
Excellence and specialised institutions, CII enables businesses to improve productivity,
quality, innovation, operational efficiency and sustainability by promoting global best
practices, knowledge sharing, capability building and collaborative learning.
CII's Centres of Excellence serve as national platforms for advancing industry
capabilities across critical areas including quality, manufacturing excellence,
logistics, green business, sustainability, water stewardship, food and agriculture,
leadership development, startups and entrepreneurship, employment and livelihoods,
skill development, and SME competitiveness.
By fostering innovation, operational excellence and responsible business practices,
CII supports enterprises of all sizes in enhancing their global competitiveness while
contributing to India's vision of sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
International Engagement
As India's engagement with the global economy continues to deepen, CII serves as a
strategic bridge between Indian industry and the international business community.
Guided by its vision of positioning Indian industry as a stable and dependable global
partner, CII works to strengthen India's international economic engagement by fostering
partnerships with governments, businesses, multilateral institutions, academia, think
tanks and industry associations worldwide.
CII's international engagement is driven through an extensive network of overseas
offices, country and regional desks, bilateral business councils, CEO forums, business
delegations, trade fairs, international conferences and strategic dialogues. With
institutional partnerships and Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) spanning business
organisations across more than 100 countries, CII creates a strong global ecosystem
for collaboration.
Through its dedicated Market Facilitation Services, CII provides end-to-end support
to businesses seeking to expand internationally by offering market intelligence,
partner identification, investment facilitation and business matchmaking services.
CII also provides policy inputs on trade agreements, market access issues, global
regulatory developments and emerging geopolitical trends.
Business Development
CII fosters business growth by creating platforms that enable enterprises to connect,
collaborate, innovate and expand. Through a wide spectrum of industry-led initiatives,
CII brings together enterprises, policymakers, investors, academia, technology
providers and global partners to exchange knowledge, forge partnerships and explore
new market opportunities.
CII organises conferences, seminars, executive dialogues, training programmes and
capacity-building initiatives addressing emerging business trends, technological
advancements, regulatory developments and sector-specific challenges. These platforms
facilitate knowledge exchange, leadership development and peer learning while enabling
enterprises to adopt global best practices.
As India's largest organiser of trade fairs and business exhibitions, CII provides
platforms that showcase the strengths of Indian industry, promote innovation and
facilitate domestic and international business engagement. CII further strengthens
business development through buyer-seller meets, B2B and B2G meetings, supplier and
vendor development initiatives, investment facilitation and market linkage programmes.
Community Development
CII believes that sustainable economic progress must be inclusive, equitable and
socially responsible. As a catalyst for nation-building, CII partners with government,
industry, civil society, academic institutions and development organisations to address
critical social and developmental challenges and contribute to India's inclusive growth
agenda and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
CII's community development initiatives span a wide range of focus areas including
education, public health, nutrition, skill development and livelihoods, women
empowerment, rural development, affirmative action, diversity and inclusion,
environmental sustainability, climate resilience, water resource management, waste
management, support for persons with disabilities, youth development and sports.
A key pillar of CII's social development efforts is the CII Foundation,
established in 2011 to drive high-impact, scalable development programmes through
collaborative partnerships with governments, corporates, civil society organisations
and local communities. Guided by its vision of "Enabling Industry for Infusing
Inclusive Development," the Foundation designs and implements programmes in areas
such as early childhood education, healthcare, women empowerment, skilling and
livelihoods, disaster relief, climate resilience, waterbody restoration, tree
plantation and waste management.
CII also champions inclusive development through initiatives that encourage greater
participation of underrepresented communities in economic growth. Together, these
efforts reinforce CII's commitment to ensuring that economic progress translates into
meaningful improvements in the quality of life for communities, creating shared value
for industry and society alike.

Corporate Governance
Corporate governance is central to building resilient, responsible and globally competitive enterprises. In today's rapidly evolving business environment—characterised by technological disruption, sustainability imperatives, heightened stakeholder expectations, geopolitical uncertainties, and increasing regulatory scrutiny—strong governance has become a strategic driver of long-term value creation, investor confidence, and business resilience.
Governance today extends beyond regulatory compliance. It encompasses ethical leadership, board effectiveness, sound risk management, transparency, accountability, stakeholder engagement, and responsible decision-making. As businesses navigate emerging issues such as ESG, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital transformation, and supply chain resilience, robust governance frameworks are essential for sustaining trust and competitiveness.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has been at the forefront of advancing corporate governance in India for over two decades. CII's pioneering Desirable Corporate Governance: A Code (1998) was the country's first voluntary corporate governance code developed by an industry association. It laid the foundation for many subsequent governance reforms and established CII's leadership in promoting global standards of corporate governance in India. Through successive reports, policy recommendations, and thought leadership initiatives, CII has consistently encouraged companies to adopt governance practices that go beyond statutory requirements and reflect the highest standards of integrity, accountability, and transparency.
CII works closely with government, regulators, industry, investors, independent directors, governance professionals, and academia to strengthen India's corporate governance ecosystem. The Institute has played an important role in shaping the policy discourse by engaging constructively with policymakers and regulators on governance-related legislation, regulatory reforms, securities market regulations, and ease of doing business. CII continues to advocate a balanced regulatory framework that promotes responsible corporate conduct while encouraging innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainable business growth.
A strong proponent of voluntary adoption of best practices and self-regulation, CII believes that effective governance is best achieved by embedding ethical values and responsible business conduct into organisational culture rather than through compliance alone. It therefore focuses on creating awareness, building institutional capacity, and equipping boards and senior management with practical guidance to address emerging governance challenges.
Through its Corporate Governance Council, national conferences, board leadership programmes, publications, research, policy advocacy, and knowledge platforms, CII provides a forum for dialogue and dissemination of global and Indian best practices. These initiatives help companies strengthen board effectiveness, enhance governance capabilities, improve risk oversight, and build organisations that are transparent, accountable, and future-ready.
By fostering excellence in corporate governance, CII remains committed to supporting businesses in creating sustainable value for shareholders and stakeholders alike, while contributing to India's aspiration of becoming a trusted, globally competitive, and responsible economy.

Ease of Doing Business
Creating a competitive, transparent and investor-friendly business environment is critical to India's aspiration of becoming a global manufacturing and investment hub. Over the past decade, the Government of India has undertaken wide-ranging reforms to simplify regulatory processes, promote digital governance, reduce compliance burden, enhance transparency, and facilitate faster approvals across the business lifecycle. These reforms span business entry, operations, expansion and exit, and are aimed at improving the overall ease of doing business for enterprises of all sizes.
India continues to pursue an ambitious reform agenda through initiatives focused on reducing regulatory compliance, decriminalising minor business-related laws, improving logistics and infrastructure, strengthening contract enforcement, streamlining approvals through digital platforms, and fostering a predictable and efficient regulatory ecosystem. These efforts are complemented by close collaboration between the Central and State Governments to drive continuous improvements in the investment climate.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), through its Task Force on Ease of Doing Business, works closely with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministries, regulatory bodies and State Governments to support the design, implementation and assessment of business reforms. CII serves as a bridge between industry and government by facilitating structured dialogue, identifying reform priorities, documenting industry feedback and promoting best practices that enhance India's business competitiveness.
CII's Ease of Doing Business initiatives are focused on:
Collaborating with Central and State Governments to strengthen the business and investment ecosystem.
Identifying priority areas for regulatory and procedural reforms through evidence-based policy advocacy.
Assessing the implementation and impact of business reforms and providing industry feedback.
Supporting compliance reduction, process simplification and digital transformation initiatives.
Building awareness among businesses on new reforms through publications, workshops, consultations and conferences.
Undertaking research and benchmarking studies on key Ease of Doing Business themes.
Strengthening the capacity of State Governments through knowledge sharing and technical support.
Providing a continuous platform for industry-government engagement to address implementation challenges and recommend future reforms.
By fostering collaborative policy dialogue and supporting reform implementation, CII remains committed to enabling a more efficient, competitive and globally attractive business environment that accelerates investment, innovation and sustainable economic growth in India.

India continues to be one of the world's fastest-growing major economies, driven by strong domestic demand, expanding investment, technological innovation, and an evolving policy landscape. The Economic Affairs Department at the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) serves as a vital interface between industry and Government, contributing to India's economic reform and growth agenda. The Department closely monitors macroeconomic trends, fiscal and monetary developments, trade and investment policies, and emerging business challenges to facilitate informed policy dialogue and evidence-based recommendations.
Through consultations, policy roundtables, seminars, conferences, and workshops at the national and regional levels, the Department brings together policymakers, industry leaders, economists, and other stakeholders to deliberate on key economic issues and shape policy outcomes. It also works extensively on direct and indirect taxation, tax administration, and regulatory reforms, providing constructive industry feedback to support a transparent, predictable, and globally competitive tax ecosystem.
CII undertakes comprehensive economic research to generate evidence-based insights that support informed policymaking and business decision-making. Its research spans macroeconomic trends, fiscal and monetary developments, trade and investment, competitiveness, emerging global economic challenges, and sectoral issues, providing industry with timely analysis of the evolving economic landscape. Through flagship publications such as the Economy Dashboard, Economy Matters, Economy Update, Business Outlook Survey, and other research reports, CII disseminates actionable insights, tracks business sentiment, and presents industry perspectives on key policy issues. These knowledge resources serve as valuable reference points for policymakers, businesses, academia, and other stakeholders, contributing to policy discourse and advancing India's agenda for sustainable, inclusive, and globally competitive economic growth.

Financial Services
India's financial services sector is a key driver of the country's economic growth, enabling capital formation, supporting businesses, fostering innovation, and promoting financial inclusion. As the economy continues to expand, supported by policy reforms, digital transformation, and increasing investor confidence, the financial services ecosystem has emerged as one of the most dynamic and resilient sectors, encompassing banking, insurance, capital markets, mutual funds, fintech, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), and wealth management.
The sector has witnessed significant growth, driven by a stable macroeconomic environment, rising domestic consumption, expanding digital infrastructure, and increasing participation from both domestic and global investors. Continued policy initiatives, regulatory reforms, and growing foreign investments have further strengthened India's position as one of the world's fastest-growing financial markets. Increasing financial literacy, rapid adoption of digital payments, and the expansion of formal financial services have accelerated financial inclusion across urban and rural India alike.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) serves as a strategic partner to the financial services ecosystem by fostering collaboration between industry, regulators, policymakers, and other stakeholders. Through policy advocacy, thought leadership, research, capacity building, industry forums, and knowledge-sharing platforms, CII works to promote a robust, transparent, innovative, and globally competitive financial sector.
CII actively engages with stakeholders across banking, insurance, capital markets, asset management, fintech, and allied financial services to address emerging opportunities and challenges. By facilitating dialogue on regulatory developments, technology adoption, risk management, sustainability, governance, and customer-centric innovation, CII supports the sector in building resilience, enhancing competitiveness, and contributing to India's vision of becoming a developed economy.

Taxation
A transparent, stable, and globally competitive tax regime is fundamental to fostering economic growth, attracting investment, and enhancing the competitiveness of Indian industry. A well-designed taxation framework supports ease of doing business, encourages innovation, facilitates trade, and provides the fiscal foundation for sustainable and inclusive development.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) works closely with the Central and State Governments, tax authorities, policymakers, and industry to promote a predictable, efficient, and business-friendly tax ecosystem. As a trusted interface between industry and government, CII represents the collective voice of business while contributing to tax policy reforms that strengthen India's competitiveness and investment climate.
CII actively monitors developments in direct and indirect taxation, tax administration, and the evolving global tax landscape. Through research, policy papers, stakeholder consultations, seminars, conferences, roundtables, and workshops, the Taxation Department facilitates constructive dialogue between government and industry, helping shape practical, transparent, and growth-oriented tax policies.
A key pillar of CII's engagement is its annual Pre-Budget and Post-Budget Memoranda, which present industry recommendations on fiscal and taxation matters to support informed policymaking. CII has also played an important role in advancing reforms relating to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Customs, contributing to policy refinement, smoother implementation, trade facilitation, and simplified compliance through sustained engagement with policymakers and tax administrators.
Through evidence-based advocacy, collaborative engagement, and policy leadership, CII remains committed to supporting a modern, efficient, and globally aligned taxation system that promotes investment, strengthens business confidence, and contributes to India's long-term economic growth and global competitiveness.

CII Research
About CII Research
In a global economy facing uncertainty from persistent geopolitical tensions, rising trade protectionism, and tariff uncertainties, India has navigated global headwinds with remarkable resilience while sustaining an impressive growth trajectory. As per MoSPI's estimates, the Indian economy grew by 7.7 per cent in FY26, supported by a sharp recovery in private consumption expenditure, which accelerated to 7.7 per cent from 5.8 per cent in the previous year. The resurgence in consumption was driven by strong rural demand, supported by a buoyant agricultural sector. A favourable monsoon led to higher agricultural output and stable food prices, strengthening household purchasing power while keeping inflation contained. Together, robust consumption and strong agricultural performance emerged as key pillars of India's growth momentum, offsetting the moderation in manufacturing growth.
Looking ahead, the outlook for the Indian economy in FY27 faces some external headwinds but is supported by resilient domestic fundamentals. The emerging El Niño conditions pose a risk to rainfall outlook and distribution and could affect agricultural output. The progress of the monsoon and kharif sowing will remain critical in shaping rural demand, inflation, and overall consumption in the coming months. India also continues to benefit from strong macroeconomic buffers, including robust services exports, comfortable foreign exchange reserves, adequate buffers in the financial system and strong domestic demand.
On the policy front, the government's continued focus on structural reforms, higher government capital expenditure, improvements in the ease of doing business, and infrastructure creation, complemented by a revival in private investment, is expected to strengthen growth prospects. In addition, India's expanding network of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) is expected to improve market access for Indian exporters, enhance global value chain integration, and attract greater foreign investment, providing further support to growth. Together, these factors are expected to support domestic demand and reinforce India's growth trajectory over the medium term, although weather-related risks and an uncertain global environment require close monitoring.

Agriculture
Agriculture remains a cornerstone of the Indian economy, contributing significantly to food security, rural livelihoods, employment, and inclusive economic growth. The sector supports nearly half of India's workforce and plays a vital role in ensuring nutritional security while supplying raw materials to several key industries. With a diverse agro-climatic landscape, abundant natural resources, and a strong scientific and research ecosystem, India has emerged as one of the world's leading producers of cereals, fruits, vegetables, milk, spices and several other agricultural commodities.
As India advances towards becoming a developed economy, agriculture is undergoing a structural transformation driven by technology adoption, climate resilience, digital innovation, mechanisation, value addition, and market integration. Government initiatives aimed at promoting sustainable farming, improving agricultural infrastructure, strengthening Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), enhancing access to finance, expanding agri-logistics, and encouraging agri-startups are creating new opportunities for farmers and agribusinesses alike. At the same time, challenges relating to productivity, climate variability, efficient resource utilisation, post-harvest losses, and market access continue to require collaborative and innovative solutions.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), through its National Council on Agriculture, works closely with the Government, industry, research institutions, startups, farmer organisations and other stakeholders to develop policy recommendations and promote initiatives that enhance the competitiveness, sustainability and resilience of India's agriculture sector. CII provides a platform for dialogue, knowledge exchange and partnerships that foster innovation across the agricultural value chain.
The Council focuses on key priority areas, including:
Promoting policy reforms to enhance agricultural competitiveness, ease of doing business and private sector participation.
Accelerating the adoption of modern technologies, precision agriculture, digital solutions and innovation across the agri-value chain.
Advancing climate-resilient and sustainable agricultural practices, efficient water management and natural resource conservation.
Strengthening agri-infrastructure, post-harvest management, food processing and value addition to improve farmers' incomes.
Enhancing market linkages, exports and integration of farmers with domestic and global value chains.
Supporting the growth of agri-startups, agri-fintech, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and entrepreneurship in rural India.
Building skills and capacity across the agricultural ecosystem through knowledge sharing, training and industry partnerships.
Facilitating collaboration among government, industry, academia and development partners to drive inclusive and sustainable agricultural growth.
CII remains committed to supporting a future-ready agriculture sector that is productive, sustainable, technology-driven and globally competitive, while improving the livelihoods of farmers and contributing to India's food and economic security.
